```{r housekeeping}

# read scoring master file

sample_categories <- read_xlsx("../../data/raw/metamethod review/master coding/codebook_categorizations.xlsx")

```

## Indeterminable Values by Variable and Study Type

```{r proc1}

# select relevant variables from data frame sample_categories
samples <- sample_categories %>% 
  select(article_id, category, info)

# join procedures_data with samples 
procedures_by_category <- procedures_data %>% 
  left_join(samples, by = "article_id") %>%
  mutate(clinical = category == 1) 

# count the tasks with clinical and non-clinical samples
row_counts <- procedures_by_category %>%
  count(clinical)

# select variables of interest
# create a boolean variable for clinical vs. non-clinical studies
# count the number of indeterminables for each variable
indeterminables_by_cat <- procedures_by_category %>%
  select(7:29, clinical) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 1:23, 
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>% 
  filter(value == "indeterminable") %>%
  count(clinical, variable) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = clinical, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(count_clinical = `TRUE`, count_non_clinical = `FALSE`) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_clinical = (count_clinical / 53 * 100),
    pct_non_clinical = (count_non_clinical / 53 * 100)
  ) %>%
  select(variable, count_clinical, pct_clinical, count_non_clinical, pct_non_clinical)

# calculate the totals across all variables
total_ind <- indeterminables_by_cat %>%
  summarise(
    variable = "total",
    count_clinical = sum(count_clinical),
    pct_clinical = (sum(count_clinical) / (53 * 23)) * 100, 
    count_non_clinical = sum(count_non_clinical),
    pct_non_clinical = (sum(count_non_clinical) / (53 * 23)) * 100
  )

# bind the total row to the main table
indeterminables_by_cat <- bind_rows(indeterminables_by_cat, total_ind)

indeterminables_by_cat |>
  kable() |>
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)

# in a next step, we want to collapse some of the variables
# determine the total number of studies
total_clinical <- row_counts$n[row_counts$clinical == TRUE]
total_non_clinical <- row_counts$n[row_counts$clinical == FALSE]

# generate the grouped table with the correct count of unique studies
indeterminables_grouped <- procedures_by_category %>%
  select(article_id, 7:29, clinical) %>%
  # rename some variables
  rename(`starting capital` = starting_capital, 
       `number of trials` = n_trials) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(article_id, clinical), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(value == "indeterminable", variable != "protocol", variable != "n_blocks") %>%
  # group variables 
  mutate(variable = case_when(
    variable %in% c("reward_disadv", "reward_adv") ~ "reward per card",
    variable %in% c("loss1", "loss2", "gain1", "gain2") ~ "gain/loss per 10 cards",
    variable %in% c("loss_int1", "loss_int2", "gain_int1", "gain_int2") ~ "gain/loss interval",
    str_detect(variable, "freq") ~ "loss frequency",
    TRUE ~ variable
  )) %>%
  # count studies per group
  group_by(clinical, variable) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(article_id), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  # wide format
  pivot_wider(names_from = clinical, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(count_clinical = `TRUE`, count_non_clinical = `FALSE`) %>%
  # calculate percentages
  mutate(
    pct_clinical = round((count_clinical / total_clinical * 100), 2),
    pct_non_clinical = round((count_non_clinical / total_non_clinical * 100), 2)
  ) %>%
  select(variable, count_clinical, pct_clinical, count_non_clinical, pct_non_clinical) %>%
  arrange(pmax(pct_clinical, pct_non_clinical))

# bind rows
# select relevant variables
indeterminables_grouped_final <- indeterminables_grouped %>%
  select(variable, pct_clinical, pct_non_clinical)

# print table
indeterminables_grouped_final |>
  kable() |>
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)

# among clinical studies, count how many used the clinical IGT variant (Bechara, 2007)
procedures_by_category %>%
  filter(clinical == TRUE) %>%
  count(variant)

```

### Plot 1

```{r proc2}

# Filter out the "total" row for better visualization
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_grouped_final %>%
  filter(variable != "total") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct_"), 
    names_to = "sample_type", 
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_type = recode(sample_type,
                         "pct_clinical" = "Clinical",
                         "pct_non_clinical" = "Non-Clinical")
  )

# sort percentages of interderminables in descending order
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_dot_data %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(max_percentage = max(percentage, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, max_percentage, .desc = FALSE))

# Create the dot plot
plot1 <- ggplot(indeterminables_dot_data, 
                aes(x = percentage, y = variable, color = sample_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Study Type",
    values = c("Clinical" = "#31688E", "Non-Clinical" = "#35B779")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Percentage of Indeterminable Values",
    y = "Variable"
  )  +
  theme_bw() + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(plot1)

ggsave(
  "figure1_indeterminables_by_variable_colors.pdf", 
  plot = plot1,                         
  width = 8,                                 
  height = 6                                 
)

ggsave(
  "figure1_indeterminables_by_variable_colors.png",
  plot = plot1,                         
  width = 8,                                 
  height = 6,                                
  dpi = 600                                  
)

```

### Plot 1 with Modified Design for Paper

```{r plots for paper}

# okabe-ito orange and blue: distinguishable in colour, greyscale, and for common colourblindness types
# shape is added so clinical vs. non-clinical remain separable in black-and-white print
plot1_grey <- ggplot(indeterminables_dot_data,
                aes(x = percentage, y = variable, color = sample_type, shape = sample_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Study Type",
                     values = c("Clinical" = "#E69F00", "Non-Clinical" = "#0072B2")) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Study Type",
                     values = c("Clinical" = 16, "Non-Clinical" = 17)) +
  labs(
    x = "Percentage of indeterminable values",
    y = "Variable"
  )  +
  theme_bw() + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


print(plot1_grey)

ggsave(
  "figure1_indeterminables_by_variable.pdf", 
  plot = plot1_grey,                         
  width = 8,                                 
  height = 6                                 
)

ggsave(
  "figure1_indeterminables_by_variable.png",
  plot = plot1_grey,                         
  width = 8,                                 
  height = 6,                                
  dpi = 600                                  
)


```

### Plot 2

```{r proc3}

# Prepare the data for plotting
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_grouped %>%
  filter(variable != "total") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct_"), 
    names_to = "sample_type", 
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_type = recode(sample_type,
                         "pct_clinical" = "Clinical",
                         "pct_non_clinical" = "Non-Clinical")
  )

# Create the dot plot
plot2 <- ggplot(indeterminables_dot_data, 
                aes(x = sample_type, y = percentage, color = variable)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Variable") +
  labs(
    title = "Indeterminable Values by Variable and Study Type",
    x = "Sample Type",
    y = "Percentage of Indeterminable Values"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1))  # Show y-axis as percentages

print(plot2)

```
